source_text:
Hymnus
ΓΕΩΡΓΙΟΙΟ ΑΛΙΤΡΟΙΟ ΥΜΝΟΣ
Μνώεο, Χριστέ, υἱὲ θεοῖο ὑψιμέδοντος, οἰκέτεω σέο κῆρ' ἀλιτροῖο γράψαντος
τάδε· καί μοι ὄπασσον λῦσιν παθέων κηριτρεφέων, τά μοι ἐμφύει ψυχᾷ ῥυπαρᾷ· δὸς
δὲ ἰδέσθαι, σῶτερ Ἰησοῦ, ζαθέαν αἴγλαν σάν· ἔνθα φανεὶς μέλψω ἀοιδὰν ψυχᾶν
παίονι, παίονι γυίων πατρὶ σὺν μεγάλῳ πνεύματι θ' ἁγνῷ.
orientation: The poet Georgius, calling himself a sinner, prays to Christ for release from passions and for vision of divine light so he may sing praise.
pass_a_gloss: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, the heart of your servant, a sinner, who has written these things; and grant me release from heart-bred passions, which grow in my impure soul; and grant me to see, Savior Jesus, your holy radiance; appearing there, I may sing a healing song for souls, healing for limbs, to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

Glossary English for the poet's self-description.
Glossary English for the inner afflictions.
Glossary English for the defiled soul.

Glossary English for the curative quality of the song.

pass_b_english: Christ, Son of the most high God, remember your servant's heart—a sinner's heart—that has written these lines. Grant me release from the heart-bred passions growing in my impure soul. And grant me, Savior Jesus, to see your holy radiance, so that, appearing in that light, I may sing a healing song for souls and limbs to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.
